Metering and cost ​

The principle: bill what vendors bill you ​

Metering is pass-through cost attribution, not a token-count product. A turn produces vendor cost lines — LLM tokens by bucket per model, speech-to-text seconds, paid lookups — each priced at the endpoint's own rate (LLM_<NAME>_PRICE, AGENT_STT_PRICE_PER_MIN). Work served from your own infrastructure costs nothing and is recorded as such: a prompt-cache hit is billed at the provider's cache-read rate because the provider bills it; a runtime-answered turn (no model call) is free; a semantic cache you built yourself is free.

The unit users see: a percentage ​

Users never see tokens, and never "N things left" (a job's cost varies 2–5× with how it goes). Caps count plan tokens — a cost-weighted token count (fresh input 1, cached read 0.1, output 6, cache write 1 by default: a typical primary model's price ratios) — because measured on real chats it tracks the bill with r = 1.00 where raw totals varied 2.4× and billable-only counts 8.9×. The widget shows "Daily · 33% used · resets in 24h". Weights are environment (AGENT_PLAN_WEIGHT_*), fixed to the primary model so a failover premium is never charged to the user.

Where the numbers live ​

  • Per call: the chain tags each model reply with provider, model and USD cost (price table or override); the chat span carries gen_ai.usage.* and gen_ai.usage.cost.
  • Per session: session.usage (four buckets, calls, turns, cost_usd, last provider/model).
  • Per turn: usage_events ledger (Mongo or JSONL under .data/ledger/): tokens, plan tokens, cost, provider, model, tool calls, whether the runtime answered.
  • Caps: Redis fixed windows (5h / day / week) + a calendar month per subject (the verified user id hashed, else the session) — usage-caps.ts.
  • A metering service (optional): AGENT_METERING_URL makes the gateway POST batched events through @marg-adk/metering — buffered, idempotent (event_id = session:turn:kind), fail-open; check(account) on the hot path bounded to 300 ms. The service rates events against a catalogue, keeps a durable ledger, and feeds a billing engine (plans, wallets, invoices) — e.g. Lago (AGPL, self-hosted) — never the agent.

Rules for emitters ​

  • No PII, no content in events — opaque ids and enums only; events are retained for years.
  • A deterministic event_id wherever your code may retry.
  • Omit vendor_cost when no third party charged for the work.
  • One event per token bucket per model call when you need per-model invoices; one per turn when a blended rate is enough.

Cost levers, in order of effect ​

  1. The cached prefix dominates: keep the system prompt byte-identical per domain × type.
  2. Load only the in-play variant's skills and tools (the typed prompt): −56% prompt size.
  3. A typed decision instead of a model call wherever a decision will do (routing, readers).
  4. Runtime-owned steps: a tap read in code costs no tokens at all.
  5. Two-stage tool-output trimming; tool results re-fetched on demand.
  6. Compare models on blended ₹/$ per million under YOUR prefix profile, never list price.
